item.title: Eastern North Pacific Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
000
ABPZ20 KNHC 270527
TWOEP

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
1100 PM PDT Sat Sep 26 2026

For the eastern and central North Pacific east of 180 longitude:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Hurricane
Polo, located southwest of Cabo San Lucas, Mexico, on Hurricane
Odalys, located well west of the southern tip of Baja California,
and on Hurricane Nolo, located south-southwest of the Big Island of
Hawaii.

Southwest of the Gulf of Tehuantepec (EP90):
Recent satellite-derived wind data indicate that the area of low
pressure located a few hundred miles southwest of the Gulf of
Tehuantepec is gradually becoming better defined. Additional
development of the system is anticipated due to conducive
environmental conditions, and a tropical depression is expected to
form in the next day or so. This system is forecast to continue
moving slowly to the west-northwest or northwest, staying parallel
to the coast of southern and southwestern Mexico. For additional
information, including Gale Warnings, see High Seas forecast issued
by the National Weather Service.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...high...90 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...high...90 percent.

Well East-Southeast of the Hawaiian Islands:
A broad area of low pressure located about 1000 miles to the
east-southeast of the Hawaiian Islands is becoming organized.
Environmental conditions are expected to be conducive for
development of this system, and a tropical depression is likely to
form during the early to middle part of next week. The system should
move generally northeastward, and remain well east-southeast of the
Hawaiian Islands.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...medium...40 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...high...70 percent.

&&

High Seas Forecasts issued by the National Weather Service
can be found under AWIPS header NFDHSFEPI, WMO header FZPN02
KWBC, and on the web at ocean.weather.gov/shtml/NFDHSFEPI.php

$$
Forecaster Pierce/Evans/Pasch

WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 200 AM PDT (0900 UTC), the center of Hurricane Odalys was located 
near latitude 21.9 North, longitude 123.4 West. Odalys is moving 
toward the north near 8 mph (13 km/h) and this motion is expected to 
prevail through this evening, followed by a sharp turn to the 
south-southeast by early next week.
 
Maximum sustained winds have decreased to near 75 mph (120 km/h) 
with higher gusts. Rapid weakening is forecast over the next few 
days, and Odalys is anticipated to become a post-tropical cyclone by 
Monday.
 
Hurricane-force winds extend outward up to 10 miles (20 km) from the
center and tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 105 miles
(165 km).
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 985 mb (29.09 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
None.

-------------

item.title: Hurricane Odalys Forecast Discussion Number 30
item.description:
Issued at 200 AM PDT Sun Sep 27 2026 
000
WTPZ41 KNHC 270855
TCDEP1
 
Hurricane Odalys Discussion Number  30
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP162026
200 AM PDT Sun Sep 27 2026

Odalys remains a low-end Category 1 hurricane, but continues to 
rapidly weaken. The system's overall convective structure has 
degenerated into an irregularly shaped central dense overcast, with 
cloud-top temperatures ranging between -65°C and -70°C just north of 
the center. The latest subjective Dvorak CI number from TAFB was 
4.5/77 kt, but the final T-number was 3.5/55 kt, which aligns better 
with the objective intensity estimates from UW-CIMSS ranging between 
53 and 65 kt, further suggesting Odalys' weakening trend. Based on a 
blend of these data, the initial intensity is lowered to 65 kt.  
The ASCAT from around 0435Z still had 57 kt vectors, and given the 
low bias of ASCAT at those wind speeds, this supports keeping 
Odalys a hurricane for this advisory.

The initial motion is estimated to be northward at 360/7 kt. Little 
change has been made to the track reasoning, as Odalys is expected 
to continue northward while a deep-layer trough steers the 
vertically coherent cyclone. Once the system decouples, motion is 
forecast to turn abruptly south-southeastward in 24 to 36 hours 
under the steering influence of a low-level ridge positioned to the 
northwest. The latest track guidance from the HCCA and GDMI ensemble 
consensus aids demonstrates a sharper turn southeastward, and the 
updated NHC track forecast reflects this while closely following the 
previous advisory.

Over the next few days, Odalys will face an increasingly hostile 
environment marked by persistent vertical wind shear, dry 
surrounding air, and significantly cooler ocean temperatures. As a 
result, rapid weakening is expected throughout the forecast period. 
Both the GFS and ECMWF simulated satellite models indicate Odalys 
will transition to a post-tropical cyclone as early as 24 hours.
 
Distant moisture from both Hurricanes Odalys and Polo will be
transported into the southwestern United States late this weekend
and early next week, and may indirectly contribute to a heavy
rainfall and flash flood threat in the region. See products issued
by the Weather Prediction Center for more information.

item.description:

...NEW WATCHES AND WARNINGS ISSUED FOR PORTIONS OF BAJA CALIFORNIA
AND MAINLAND NORTHWESTERN MEXICO...
...PREPARATIONS TO PROTECT LIFE AND PROPERTY SHOULD BE RUSHED TO
COMPLETION IN BAJA CALIFORNIA SUR...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 200 AM MST...0900 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...20.3N 113.6W
ABOUT 300 MI...480 KM SW OF CABO SAN LUCAS MEXICO
ABOUT 320 MI...520 KM SSW OF CABO SAN LAZARO MEXICO
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...120 MPH...195 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...NNW OR 330 DEGREES AT 10 MPH...17 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...952 MB...28.12 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
CHANGES WITH THIS ADVISORY:
 
The government of Mexico has issued a Hurricane Warning along the
east coast of Baja California Sur from Loreto to Santa Rosalia
 
The government of Mexico has issued a Hurricane Watch along the 
coast of mainland Mexico from Huatabampito to Bahia Kino.
 
The government of Mexico has issued a Tropical Storm Warning along
the east coast of Baja California Sur south of Loreto to San
Evaristo.
 
The government of Mexico has issued a Tropical Storm Warning along
the east coast of Baja California Sur north of Santa Rosalia to
Bahia San Juan Batista.
 
The government of Mexico has issued a Tropical Storm Watch in
mainland Mexico south of Huatabampito to Topolobampo.
 
SUMMARY OF WATCHES AND WARNINGS IN EFFECT:
 
A Hurricane Warning is in effect for...
* West coast of Baja California Sur, from Punta Abreojos to Santa Fe
* East coast of Baja California Sur, from Loreto to Santa Rosalia
 
A Hurricane Watch is in effect for...
* West coast of Baja California Sur, north of Punta Abreojos to
Punta Eugenia
* East coast of Baja California Sur, south of Loreto to San
Evaristo
* East coast of Baja California Sur, north of Santa Rosalia to
Bahia San Juan Bautista
* Mainland Mexico from Huatabampito to Bahia Kino
 
A Tropical Storm Warning is in effect for...
* West coast of Baja California Sur, north of Punta Abreojos to
Punta Eugenia.
* East coast of Baja California Sur, north of Santa Rosalia to
Bahia San Juan Bautista
* East coast of Baja California Sur, south of Loreto to San
Evaristo.
 
A Tropical Storm Watch is in effect for...
* Mainland Mexico south of Huatabampito to Topolobampo
 
A Hurricane Warning means that hurricane conditions are expected
somewhere within the warning area.  A warning is typically issued 36
hours before the anticipated first occurrence of
tropical-storm-force winds, conditions that make outside
preparations difficult or dangerous.  Preparations to protect life
and property should be rushed to completion.
 
A Hurricane Watch means that hurricane conditions are possible
within the watch area.  A watch is typically issued 48 hours before
the anticipated first occurrence of tropical-storm-force winds,
conditions that make outside preparations difficult or dangerous.
 
A Tropical Storm Warning means that tropical storm conditions are
expected somewhere within the warning area, generally within 36
hours.
 
A Tropical Storm Watch means that tropical storm conditions are
possible within the watch area, generally within 48 hours.
 
Interests in the remainder of Baja California Sur, and the remainder
of Sonora and northern Sinaloa should monitor the progress of Polo.
 
For storm information specific to your area, please monitor
products issued by your national meteorological service.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 200 AM MST (0900 UTC), the center of Hurricane Polo was located
near latitude 20.3 North, longitude 113.6 West. Polo is moving
toward the north-northwest near 10 mph (17 km/h). A turn toward the
north is expected later today, followed by a turn toward the
northeast on Monday. On the forecast track, Polo is expected to
approach the west coast of Baja California Sur on Monday, move
across the peninsula Monday night and then approach northwestern
mainland Mexico by early Tuesday.
 
Maximum sustained winds remain near 120 mph (195 km/h) with higher
gusts. Polo is a category 3 hurricane on the Saffir-Simpson
Hurricane Wind Scale. Additional weakening is expected during the
next few days, but Polo is forecast to remain a hurricane when it
approaches Baja California Sur on Monday.
 
Hurricane-force winds extend outward up to 45 miles (75 km) from the
center and tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 125 miles
(205 km).
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 952 mb (28.12 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
Key messages for Polo can be found in the Tropical Cyclone
Discussion under AWIPS header MIATCDEP2 and WMO header WTPZ42 KNHC.
 
WIND: Hurricane conditions are expected within the warning area
along the west coast of Baja California Sur by Monday afternoon,
with tropical storm conditions possible in the southern portion of
the warning area by tonight into early Monday. These conditions
are expected to spread northward during the day on Monday and then
eastward across Baja California Sur by Monday evening. Hurricane
conditions are possible within the Hurricane Watch area in mainland
northwestern Mexico on Tuesday.
 
RAINFALL: Polo is expected to produce rainfall totals of 4 to 8
inches with maximum amounts of 10 inches across portions of Baja
California Sur. This rainfall may produce life-threatening flooding
and mudslides, especially in areas of steep terrain.
 
For a complete depiction of forecast rainfall associated with Polo,
please see the National Weather Service Storm Total Rainfall Graphic
available at hurricanes.gov/graphics_ep2.shtml?rainqpf
 
SURGE: A storm surge could produce significant coastal flooding in
areas of onshore winds. Near the coast, the surge will be
accompanied by large and destructive waves.
 
SURF: Swells generated by Polo will continue affecting the coast of
southwestern Mexico, west-central Mexico, and Baja California Sur
during the next couple of days. These swells will spread northward
along the coast of the Baja California Peninsula through the
remainder of the weekend. These swells are likely to cause
life-threatening surf, rip currents, and coastal flooding. Please
consult products from your local weather office.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next intermediate advisory at 500 AM MST.
Next complete advisory at 800 AM MST.
 
$$
Forecaster Hagen

item.title: Hurricane Polo Forecast Discussion Number 26
item.description:
Issued at 800 PM MST Sat Sep 26 2026 
000
WTPZ42 KNHC 270245
TCDEP2
 
Hurricane Polo Discussion Number  26
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP172026
800 PM MST Sat Sep 26 2026
 
A NOAA Hurricane Hunter aircraft investigated Polo during the 
last few hours and found that although it has weakened, the system 
remains a major hurricane. The highest flight-level winds measured 
by the plane on its last pass through Polo were 114 kt, while the 
minimum pressure measured by a dropsonde was 949 mb. Based on these 
data, the intensity of Polo is set at 105 kt. The NOAA aircraft also 
confirmed that Polo's inner core has expanded, and reported that 
the eyewall of the hurricane is open on the north side of the 
circulation.

Polo is still heading northwestward, moving around the western edge 
of a mid-level ridge centered over northern Mexico. Polo will turn 
northward tomorrow, and then northeastward on Monday as it 
continues to move around the ridge and becomes increasingly 
affected by a mid- to upper-level trough moving in from the 
northwest. The largest source of uncertainty in the forecast 
continues to be the forward speed of Polo as it makes its expected 
northeastward turn between the aforementioned synoptic features. The 
model spread remains higher than unusual between 48 and 72 h, and 
confidence in this portion of the forecast is low. The NHC 
forecast is still generally close to GDM and HCCA, which are on the 
faster end of the guidance, and only minor adjustments were made to 
the official forecast with this advisory.

Continued steady weakening is expected during the next day or two 
given Polo's degraded structure and the expectation that it will 
continue to encounter moderate vertical wind shear and move into a 
drier surrounding environment. However, Polo is still expected to be 
a hurricane when it approaches Baja California Sur on Monday. 
Rapid weakening is likely once the hurricane makes landfall, and 
Polo will likely dissipate over mainland Mexico by late Tuesday. 
 
Polo is expected to become a remnant low and then dissipate before
it reaches the southern U.S., but distant moisture associated with
it and Odalys will be transported into the southwestern United
States late this weekend and early next week, and may indirectly
contribute to a heavy rainfall and flash flood threat in the region.
See products issued by the Weather Prediction Center for more
information.
 
 
Key Messages:
 
1. Polo is forecast to approach the west coast of the Baja
California peninsula on Monday as a hurricane, and a Hurricane
Warning is in effect for that region. Tropical storm conditions
could reach portions of the coast as soon as Sunday night or early
Monday, making further preparations difficult. These conditions 
will likely spread across Baja California through Monday. A storm 
surge is likely, especially in areas of onshore winds. 
 
2. Heavy rainfall associated with Polo may begin to impact Baja
California Sur Sunday night into Tuesday. This rainfall may produce
life-threatening flooding and mudslides, especially in areas of
steep terrain.
 
3. Dangerous surf and rip currents are likely along portions of
the northwest coast of Mexico and Baja California for the next
several days.

item.description:

BULLETIN
Tropical Depression Eighteen-E Advisory Number   1
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP182026
300 AM CST Sun Sep 27 2026
 
...TROPICAL DEPRESSION EIGHTEEN-E FORMS SOUTH OF MEXICO...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 300 AM CST...0900 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...12.2N 99.1W
ABOUT 330 MI...530 KM S OF ACAPULCO MEXICO
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...35 MPH...55 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...WNW OR 285 DEGREES AT 10 MPH...17 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...1008 MB...29.77 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 300 AM CST (0900 UTC), the center of Tropical Depression
Eighteen-E was located near latitude 12.2 North, longitude 99.1
West.  The depression is moving toward the west-northwest near 10 
mph (17 km/h) and this general motion is expected to prevail 
through the next several days.  On the forecast track, the center 
of the system will move parallel to and offshore of the coast of 
Mexico.
 
Maximum sustained winds are near 35 mph (55 km/h) with higher gusts.
Some gradual strengthening is forecast during the next few days, 
and the depression could become a tropical storm by tonight.
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 1008 mb (29.77 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
None
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 900 AM CST.
 
$$
Forecaster Evans/Pasch

item.title: Tropical Depression Eighteen-E Forecast Discussion Number 1
item.description:
Issued at 300 AM CST Sun Sep 27 2026 
000
WTPZ43 KNHC 270855
TCDEP3
 
Tropical Depression Eighteen-E Discussion Number   1
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP182026
300 AM CST Sun Sep 27 2026

The tropical disturbance located south of Mexico, formerly Invest 
90E, has become better organized based on satellite imagery over the 
last several hours. Scatterometry data from around 0300 UTC depicts 
a closed circulation, with the system moving into a favorable 
environment for further development. Subjective Dvorak 
intensity analysis from TAFB also rated the system at 2.0/30 kt.  
Therefore, advisories have begun for Tropical Depression 
Eighteen-E. 

The initial motion is somewhat uncertain since the cyclone has only 
recently formed, but the motion estimate is around 285/9 kt. Track 
guidance is in good agreement on steering this system generally to 
the west-northwest over the next several days, with an increase in 
forward speed as it runs south of a mid-level high over Mexico. The 
current NHC track forecast generally falls within the middle of the 
guidance envelope, favoring HCCA in particular. 

SHIPS guidance suggests that vertical wind shear may be an 
inhibiting factor for development for the first 24 h, before the 
Depression is expected to gradually strengthen as SSTs remain warm 
and mid-level moisture appears favorable. There is some uncertainty 
with regards to SSTs due to colder waters potentially being churned 
up in the wake of Hurricane Polo, so the current intensity forecast 
is a little conservative at first, before depicting gradual 
strengthening through the late weekend onward. This still falls 
around the median of the guidance envelope.
